experiment: The lid opened mid-capture, on a good copy of Omikron - The Nomad Soul (5 tracks), with the DMA engine; then resumed in the SAME boot and verified.
observed: GD-ROM DMA read did not complete (FAILED); DMA stays off until reboot
Partial job preserved: /KUI/dumps/ddef8ea0e44107842-0001 (after 37.5 s of capture)
RESUME LATEST MATCHING JOB in the same boot: CAPTURED all 5 tracks; Reference check (TOSEC): FULL TRACK MATCH
the resumed capture took 1586.7 s (26.4 minutes): PIO speed, because DMA had been switched off

pc_verification.reference_check_done_afterwards: The five sizes and CRC32s match TOSEC 'Omikron - The Nomad Soul v1.001 (2000)(Eidos)(US)(M5)[!][2S]' 5/5; the [1S] entry matches 3/5.

conclusions: The failure path works on hardware: opening the lid stopped the capture cleanly, kept the partial job, and a resume finished it byte-exact against TOSEC on the console and on the PC.
It also confirmed a flaw on hardware: any DMA read cut short switched DMA off until reboot, so the same-boot resume ran at PIO speed (26.4 minutes against about 19.6).

Two causes, both fixed: (1) the policy treated every unfinished DMA read as a DMA fault, including a stop, a disc change and a damaged sector; now only a timeout or three failures in a row on an unchanged disc turn DMA off. (2) The async read never latched a disc change (the blocking path checks the drive's sense code; the async one did not), so the change was only noticed by the PIO re-read that followed.
tests/test_disc.c now pins both (dma-async-stop, -change, -fail, -timeout); reverting either fix fails a scenario. Hardware confirmation of the fix: the next same-boot resume should keep DMA.
